questions.question: Which description fits the **Contract** resource?
options: Legally enforceable, formally recorded unilateral or bilateral directive i.e., a policy or agreement.
A financial tool for tracking value accrued for a particular purpose.
This resource provides: the claim details; adjudication details from the processing of a Claim; and optionally account balance information, for informing the subscriber of the benefits provided.
Details of a Health Insurance product/plan provided by an organization.
questions.explanation: **Contract**: Legally enforceable, formally recorded unilateral or bilateral directive i.e., a policy or agreement. The other descriptions belong to **Account**, **ExplanationOfBenefit**, **InsurancePlan**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “Legally enforceable, formally recorded unilateral or bilateral directive i.e., a policy or agreement.”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **Contract** (Financial › General).

questions.question: Where does **Contract** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **Contract** is in **Financial › General**: Other financial records: patient accounts, individual charges and their pricing, contracts, insurance plan details, and the explanation of benefits sent to patients.

questions.question: Which statement about required elements in **Contract** is true?
options: No top-level element is required: every element has a minimum cardinality of 0
questions.explanation: Every top-level element of Contract is optional (`0..1` or `0..*`) in the base resource. Profiles can make elements required for a particular use.

questions.question: Which element of **Contract** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of Contract: `status`. `status`: amended | appended | cancelled | disputed | entered-in-error | executable | executed | negotiable | offered | policy | rejected | renewed | revoked | resolved | terminated. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
